title: Study the flora in Marigold ensilage made from temple waste and evaluate the phytobiotic compounds developed
venue: Journal of Emerging Technologies and Innovative Research (JETIR)
abstract: Floral waste from religious offerings in India, predominantly marigold (Tagetes erecta), contributes significantly to municipal solid waste and river eutrophication when disposed of untreated. This research investigates the controlled anaerobic ensilage of marigold floral waste to stabilize the biomass and develop bioactive phytobiotic compounds. The succession of microflora during ensilage was isolated and characterized, identifying key lactic acid bacteria and cellulolytic fungal species. Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis verified the development of valuable antimicrobial, antioxidant, and phytobiotic compounds, demonstrating a sustainable bio-processing route for converting organic temple waste into valuable biochemical products.

title: Enhancing Learning Retention through Mind Maps, Pre-lab Worksheets and Interactive Quizzes: An Experiential Approach
abstract: Laboratory education in undergraduate microbiology often relies on linear, cookbook-style protocols that hinder deep conceptual understanding. This study presents a three-stage experiential framework combining visual mind maps, structured pre-laboratory preparatory worksheets, and formative interactive quizzes. Implemented across undergraduate science cohorts at SIES College of Arts, Science and Commerce, Sion, the intervention led to measurable improvements in cognitive recall (evaluated via pre/post testing), procedural safety adherence, and independent experimental troubleshooting.
apa: Chaudri, W. (2023). Enhancing Learning Retention through Mind Maps, Pre-lab Worksheets and Interactive Quizzes: An Experiential Approach. SIES Academic Research.

title: B. Sc. Semester II, Major Microbiology Course (Practical)
abstract: A comprehensive practical handbook designed for undergraduate students taking Semester II Major Microbiology under the revised university curriculum framework. Covers core aseptic techniques, differential staining protocols, serial dilution and viable cell count methodologies, microbial growth curve kinetics, enzymatic assays, and basic bioprocess instrumentation. Structured with clear learning outcomes, step-by-step bench procedures, observations tables, and viva-voce review questions.
apa: Chaudri, W. (2023). B. Sc. Semester II, Major Microbiology Course (Practical). Pune: My Rays Publishing House.

title: Use of Microflora from ensilage marigold temple waste to efficiently extract phytobiotic pigments (Xanthophyll and Carotene) and study their effect on pigmentation of catfish
venue: Department of Microbiology, SIES College of Arts, Science & Commerce (Autonomous), University of Mumbai
abstract: Doctoral dissertation investigating a closed-loop biotechnology process. Floral marigold waste collected from temple shrines in Mumbai is processed via controlled ensilage fermentation. Endogenous and inoculant microflora produce in-situ cellulases and pectinases, degrading plant cell walls to liberate natural xanthophyll (lutein) and carotene without destructive chemical inputs. The recovered phytobiotic pigment extract is evaluated for bio-stability and incorporated as a natural feed supplement in freshwater catfish aquaculture diets, measuring growth indices, flesh pigmentation, and antioxidant defense.
apa: Chaudri, W. N. (2024). Use of Microflora from ensilage marigold temple waste to efficiently extract phytobiotic pigments (Xanthophyll and Carotene) and study their effect on pigmentation of catfish (Doctoral dissertation). Department of Microbiology, SIES College, University of Mumbai.

title: Biotechnological Valorization of Floral Waste for Pigment Recovery and Sustainable Aquaculture
venue: Aavishkar: Inter-Collegiate / Inter-University Research Convention, University of Mumbai
abstract: Presented experimental findings on the dual benefits of marigold waste bio-fermentation: diverting organic waste streams away from urban water bodies in Mumbai while producing high-grade natural carotenes and xanthophylls for aquatic feed formulations. Evaluated at the institutional and university rounds of the prestigious Aavishkar convention.
apa: Chaudri, W. (2023). Biotechnological Valorization of Floral Waste for Pigment Recovery and Sustainable Aquaculture. In Proceedings of Aavishkar Research Convention. University of Mumbai.
